text:
alex: Quick pass on the FY27 OKR draft — dropped a new sheet 'launch-commitments-v2' with conservative milestones and MVP scope. link: https://tiny.redwood/okr-fy27 :spiral_calendar:

maria: looked. thanks. big question: do we keep 'latency SLO 99p < 150ms' as a company-level KR or move to infra-specific KR? feels infra-owned but product-impactful.

sam: leaning to company-level. customers care about top-line latency across hosted + dedicated. infra teams can be owners of sub-KRs.

jen: agree w/ sam. also need explicit rollback guard for model rollouts in the KR — we've seen regressions slip in without canary metrics.

ryan: +1. add a canary pass/fail metric tied to eval-set perf and error-rate. simple boolean is fine for exec readouts.

nia: noted. on the scope side, the sheet marks 'realtime embeddings cache' as must-have for Q1. that's a heavy infra dependency (redis cluster + eviction tuning). can we scope to a pilot for top 3 customers instead?

alex: good call. proposal: pilot for top 3 customers in Q1, full rollout in Q2 pending cost delta < 18%. wrote this in the 'assumptions' tab.

ina: (pm-ina) wording nit: change "top 3 customers" -> "customer pilot (3 high-usage customers)" for clarity in the OKR. also add acceptance criteria: 95% of pilot queries served from cache, end-to-end latency delta < 20ms.

sam: on prioritization — we have customer ask to support model pinning per-route. that's high-value but estimated 6 wks with eng infra support. if we accept it for Q1, we should drop either 'new-benchmark-suite' or reduce scope of 'dedicated autoscale policies'.

maria: customer pinning seems revenue-impacting (enterprise legal product teams). recommend swap: keep pinning, defer full autoscale policy features to Q2.

jen: can we split autoscale: land basic threshold-based autoscale in Q1, advanced policy engine in Q2?

sam: yes that's workable. update the sheet to reflect split.

alex: okay final asks before I lock the draft for exec review at 5pm PT:
- confirm company-level latency KR with canary metric (owner: infra/sam)
- pilot-only scope for realtime embeddings in Q1 (owner: platform/nia)
- accept per-route model pinning for Q1, autoscale split (owner: runtime/sam + infra/jen)
- add rollback/canary acceptance criteria to release playbook (owner: oncall/jen)

ryan: if those owners are committed, i'm good to sign. minor ask: add a single line about cost guardrails for hosted API (max % of gross margin impact tolerated).

alex: added cost guardrail line in 'constraints' tab. thanks all — i will publish the exec packet and tag you for sign-off. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Scheduled: exec-packet.pdf generated and added to #exec-review (link: https://tiny.redwood/exec-packet-fy27).

maria: will review before 4:30. ping if anything changes.

sam: i'll sync w/ infra standup at 10 to confirm owners and blockers.

jen: I'll add rollback checklist to the release playbook and link from the OKR doc.

alex: thanks team — locking the draft at 17:00 PT unless objections.
